Candidate edges of this concept. A misconception/error edge shows the wrong rule (logic) and the right rule (twin_logic); a concept edge shows the rule that links the two concepts; a level way (lvl:) shows one way an answer can display a level of understanding of the concept.
- lvl:logical_operators@L0#0 | level L0 way everyday_reading: Folk meaning: English 'or' is often exclusive ('tea or coffee') and 'and' can join alternatives ('x is 1 and 2' meaning either value). Java rule: || is inclusive (true when either or both operands are true) and && is true only when both operands are true, so x == 1 && x == 2 is always false.
- lvl:logical_operators@L0#4 | level L0 way inconsistent_trace: Points to LT (! first, then &&, then ||; left operand first; right operand of && / || only if needed). Applied unevenly: in one row of a trace the student evaluates the right operand of && although the left was false (or reads || as exclusive when both operands are true) and in another row applies the rule correctly. (here mixing in: "& is only a bitwise operator")
- lvl:logical_operators@L1#0 | level L1 way names_the_element: Logical (boolean) operators: && (and), || (or) and ! (not), which take boolean operands and produce a boolean.
- lvl:logical_operators@L1#1 | level L1 way states_the_rule: a && b is true if both operands are true and false otherwise; a || b is false if both are false and true otherwise; !a is the opposite of a; these definitions are given in full by truth tables.
- lvl:logical_operators@L2#0 | level L2 way line_by_line_trace: ! is applied before && and ||, and && before ||; the left operand is evaluated first, and for && and || the right operand is evaluated only when the left has not already decided the result.
- lvl:logical_operators@L2#1 | level L2 way output_prediction: The result is a boolean: with x = 10, x > 0 && x < 10 is false and x < 0 || x > 10 is false; true || anything is true.
- lvl:logical_operators@L2#2 | level L2 way one_step_execution: The operators themselves change no variable; any side effect inside the right operand (i++, a method call) happens only if that operand is evaluated.
- lvl:logical_operators@L3#0 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: Combining boolean sub-expressions with &&, || and ! yields another boolean expression, so arbitrarily complex conditions can be built with parentheses.
- lvl:logical_operators@L3#1 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: && and || are the short-circuit operators: in a guard such as (x != 0 && y / x > 1) the operand order matters, because the right test runs only when the left one allows it.
- lvl:logical_operators@L3#2 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: Comparisons bind tighter than && and ||, so comparisons are evaluated first and their boolean results are then combined (month >= 1 && month <= 12).
- lvl:logical_operators@L3#3 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: ^ on booleans is a further logical operator, true exactly when the operands differ (it equals (a || b) && !(a && b)), but unlike && and || it always evaluates both operands.
- lvl:logical_operators@L3#4 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: De Morgan's laws rewrite negated && / || expressions: !(A && B) is !A || !B and !(A || B) is !A && !B.
- lvl:logical_operators@L3#5 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: The operands must be boolean, and the result is boolean; int operands are a compile-time error.
- lvl:logical_operators@L3#6 | level L3 way purpose_of_the_whole: Used to combine several conditions into one test: a range check (lo <= x && x <= hi), alternatives (x == 0 || y == 0), a guard followed by the real test (i < n && a[i] != 0), or a rule built step by step as in LeapYear.
- lvl:logical_operators@L4#0 | level L4 way predict_a_change: Swapping && for || changes the meaning; negating a whole condition requires De Morgan (negate each term and flip the operator); swapping the operands of && or || keeps the truth value but can change which side effects or exceptions occur.
- lvl:logical_operators@L4#1 | level L4 way transfer_to_a_new_program: Use && and || to combine conditions into a single test, ordering operands so that cheap or protective tests come first; use nested ifs only when the cases need different actions; do not use & and | for conditions.
- lvl:logical_operators@L4#2 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: Conditions are combined with && and ||; & and | evaluate both operands. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: Using & or | where the right operand is only safe when the left decides first, e.g. x != 0 & y / x > 1 with x == 0 (ArithmeticException) or an out-of-range index; otherwise a silent difference only when the right side has side effects.
- lvl:logical_operators@L4#3 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: && has higher precedence than ||. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Mixed && and || without parentheses intended to group the || first, e.g. a || b && c meant as (a || b) && c.
- lvl:logical_operators@L4#4 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: Logical operators take boolean operands only. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: Applying && or || to int operands (if (x && y) with ints) or writing and/or as words.
